study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized resting-state functional connectivity abnormalities unveil two major depressive disorder subtypes with contrasting abnormal patterns of abnormality

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its research objectives: (1) to identify MDD subtypes based on subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities using a tolerance interval-based approach, (2) to assess the reproducibility and sensitivity of these subtypes, and (3) to evaluate whether these subtypes could improve case-control discriminability. The purpose of applying normative modeling is explicitly described as identifying biologically homogeneous subtypes within MDD to improve both diagnosis and treatment, addressing clinical heterogeneity.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: This study aimed to identify MDD subtypes based on subject-level functional connectivity abnormalities using a tolerance interval-based approach... We assessed the reproducibility and sensitivity of these subtypes using subsampling validation, leave-one-site-out validation, different parameter settings, and analysis restricted to untreated patients. Finally, we evaluated whether these subtypes could improve case-control discriminability. ... Identifying more biologically homogeneous subtypes within the broad clinical diagnosis of MDD may help to unravel this complexity, ultimately improving both diagnosis and treatment.

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: Following prior studies, we set a 90% tolerance proportion with a 10% confidence level [22]. Functional connections in individual subjects (both MDD and HCs) fell outside this range were classified as extreme... Out of 19,900 functional connections, 556 showed a consistency rate greater than 95%... Specifically, patients with subtype 1 only exhibited overall increased functional connectivity in 19,579 of the total 19,900 functional connections... On the contrary, patients with subtype 2 only exhibited overall decreased functional connectivity in 15,405 of the total 19,900 functional connections... We found significant enrichment in reward, motivation, and pain (all permutation p < 0.05)... Regarding clinical characteristics, extreme functional connections were significantly associated with the age of onset (adjusted R2 = 0.39, F statistic = 2.13, Bonferroni corrected p < 0.01)... This study has several limitations. First, only cross-sectional data were analyzed... Second, the limited clinical data available prevented us from examining other potential differences between subtypes...
